findings.title: Surface-area expansion mistakes a fractional quantity for a denominator
findings.problem: The new slash rule runs without checking what precedes the slash. It rewrites a numeric fraction followed by square meters as "per", changing the quantity's meaning rather than merely expanding its notation. The audio gate cannot catch this because it checks the already-rewritten script.
findings.failure_scenario: An approved pediatric calculation stating "A child's body surface area is 3/4 m²." becomes "A child's body surface area is 3 per 4 square meters." The displayed quantity is 0.75 square meters, while the narration describes a per-area expression. Audio faithfully reading that incorrect script can pass voiceCheck.
findings.fix: Restrict this expansion to an established denominator context, such as the trailing area denominator in "mL/min/1.73 m²". Preserve bare numeric fractions followed by area units. Add regression tests asserting that fractional BSA quantities remain unchanged while the intended eGFR notation still expands correctly.

assessment: One clinical-content blocker remains: the new surface-area rewrite can change a fractional area into a reciprocal-area expression before the audio accuracy gate checks it.
